classes.name: Riigikogu valimised
classes.name_en: Riigikogu elections
classes.finest_note: The open data (2015 on) and the archive pages (1992 to 2011) give each district's votes by municipality, Tallinn city district, and polling division; e-votes and votes cast abroad are given for the whole district.
classes.note: 101 members by open-list proportional representation in 12 districts (11 in 1995 and 1999), with personal quotas, district quotas, and national compensation seats by a modified d'Hondt method among lists over 5% (Constitution § 60; Riigikogu Election Act §§ 6, 65 to 67). Regular elections are on the first Sunday in March every fourth year; an early election follows a dissolution.

classes.name: Rahvahääletused
classes.name_en: National referendums
classes.finest_note: 1992 and 2003 are published by county and city; the 1991 poll and the interwar referendums only as national totals in the sources found so far.
classes.note: The Riigikogu may put a bill or other affair of state to a referendum, whose decision binds all state bodies; Chapters I and XV of the Constitution can only be amended by referendum (Constitution §§ 105, 106, 162 to 164). The 1920 Constitution also allowed popular initiatives.
classes.locator: https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/523042025002/consolide (§ 105: "The Riigikogu has the right to submit a bill or other affairs of state to a referendum.")

classes.name: Vabariigi Presidendi valimised
classes.name_en: Presidential elections (by the Riigikogu and the electoral body)
classes.note: The Riigikogu elects the President by a two-thirds majority in up to three rounds; failing that, an electoral body of the Riigikogu and representatives of the municipal councils elects (Constitution § 79). Each round's votes are published by the State Electoral Office.

dates.note: The second round, in the Riigikogu, after the popular first round of 20 September 1992 (class president_1992).

classes.name: Riigikogu juhatuse valimised
classes.name_en: Elections of the Board of the Riigikogu (President and two Vice-Presidents)
classes.note: The new Riigikogu elects its President and two Vice-Presidents at its first sitting for one year, and again every year after; secret ballot, a majority of valid votes, a run-off between the top two. The State Electoral Office publishes each election from the 7th Riigikogu.

classes.name: Kohaliku omavalitsuse volikogu valimised
classes.name_en: Municipal council elections
classes.finest_note: Each council's electoral districts; the open data (2013 on) and the archive pages also give each polling division.
classes.note: Councils are elected for four years on the third Sunday in October by open-list proportional representation in one or more districts (eight in Tallinn); permanent residents vote, from 2026 only citizens of Estonia and the European Union (Constitution § 156; Municipal Council Election Act §§ 2, 8). Contests here are the councils' electoral districts.
classes.locator: https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/506112013004/consolide/current (§ 2: "Councils are elected for a term of four years. Council elections are held on the third Sunday in October in an election year.")

classes.name: Volikogu täiendavad valimised
classes.name_en: Supplementary municipal council elections
classes.note: Held in the districts with no alternate members left when a council falls below a quorum (Municipal Council Election Act § 3); rare, and not yet listed.

classes.name: Volikogu esimehe ja vallavanema/linnapea valimine
classes.name_en: Council chairs and mayors elected by the council
classes.disposition_reason: The council elects its chair and the mayor (vallavanem or linnapea) at a council sitting; the votes are in council minutes, not published by an electoral body.

classes.name: Linnaosa halduskogud
classes.name_en: Administrative councils of Tallinn's city districts
classes.disposition_reason: Tallinn's city district administrative councils are formed by the city council in proportion to its factions, not elected by voters.

classes.name: Külavanemad ja alevikuvanemad
classes.name_en: Village and borough elders
classes.disposition_reason: Village elders are chosen at village general meetings under each municipality's own rules; no state body runs or publishes these.

classes.name: Elanike küsitlused
classes.name_en: Municipal residents' polls
classes.disposition_reason: Estonian law provides no local referendum; the polls municipalities hold (as on mergers) are consultative and run by the municipality itself.

classes.name: Kultuurinõukogu valimised
classes.name_en: Cultural council elections of national minority cultural autonomies
classes.disposition_reason: The cultural councils of the Ingrian Finnish (2004) and Swedish (2007) cultural autonomies are elected by members on the minority's own list, in polls run by the minority's election committee; no state body publishes results.

classes.name: Kaasistujate kandidaatide valimine
classes.name_en: Lay judge candidates elected by municipal councils
classes.disposition_reason: Municipal councils elect candidates for lay judge, and a court committee appoints them; neither step is a public vote.

classes.name: Erakondade sisevalimised
classes.name_en: Party internal elections and candidate selection
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their candidates and leaders under their own statutes; the state neither runs nor publishes these.

classes.name: Asutava Kogu ja Riigikogu valimised 1919–1932
classes.name_en: Constituent Assembly and Riigikogu elections, 1919 to 1932
classes.note: The 120-member Constituent Assembly (1919) and the 100-member Riigikogu (1920 to 1932) were elected by list proportional representation in multi-member districts. Returns are in the State Statistical Central Bureau's publications.

dates.quote: The elections to the Constituent Assembly were held on 5–7 April 1919. ... The Constituent Assembly had 120 seats.
The elections of the 1st Riigikogu were held on 27–29 November 1920.
dates.note: 100 members, from the same site's description of the 1st Riigikogu.

dates.quote: The elections of the 2nd Riigikogu were held on 5–7 May 1923.
The elections of the 3rd Riigikogu were held on 15–17 May 1926.
The elections of the 4th Riigikogu were held on 11–13 May 1929.
The elections of the 5th Riigikogu were held on 21–23 May 1932.

classes.name: Rahvuskogu I koja ja Riigivolikogu valimised
classes.name_en: National Assembly First Chamber (1936) and Chamber of Deputies (1938) elections
classes.note: 80 single-member districts under martial law; the opposition boycotted 1936. The National Council (Riiginõukogu) of 1938 was partly chosen by local governments and corporate chambers and is not a class here. The July 1940 vote under Soviet occupation is not counted as an election of the Republic.

dates.quote: The elections of the First camber of the National Assembly were held on 12–14 December 1936. ... there were no elections in 50 districts ... In the remaining 30 districts
dates.note: 80 single-member districts; 50 were uncontested.

dates.quote: The elections of the 6th Riigikogu were held on 24–25 February 1938. ... The 80 members of the Chamber of Deputies were elected in general elections based on the majority principle.

classes.name: Riigipea valimine 1938
classes.name_en: Election of the President of the Republic, 1938
classes.note: Under the 1938 Constitution the President was elected by an electoral assembly of both chambers and local government representatives; held once, in April 1938. The 1934 State Elder election under the 1933 Constitution was called off under martial law.

classes.name: Valla- ja linnavolikogude valimised 1918–1939
classes.name_en: Rural municipality and city council elections, 1918 to 1939
classes.note: Rural municipality and city councils were elected under the Republic's local government laws; returns are in the State Statistical Central Bureau's publications and the official gazette, not yet located online.

classes.name: Eesti NSV Ülemnõukogu valimised 1990
classes.name_en: Supreme Council election, 1990
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of the 1990 results by district has been found online; the returns are in the National Archives and the gazette of the time.
classes.note: 105 seats by single transferable vote; four seats were reserved for the Soviet armed forces.

dates.quote: The elections of the 12th Supreme Council of the Republic of Estonia were held on 18 March 1990. ... 392 persons stood as candidates for the 105 seats of the Supreme Council

classes.name: Eesti NSV Ülemnõukogu ja kohalike nõukogude valimised 1940–1989
classes.name_en: Supreme Soviet and local soviet elections of the Estonian SSR, 1940 to 1989
classes.disposition_reason: Single-list elections under Soviet occupation; no official list of dates or returns has been found online. Elections to all-Union bodies belong to the Soviet Union, not to this census.

classes.name: Eesti Kongressi valimised 1990
classes.name_en: Congress of Estonia election, 1990
classes.disposition_reason: Organized by the citizens' committees among registered citizens of the Republic, not by a state body; no state publication.
